messages:
Maya (GaleHealth): Hey team — we started seeing a spike of 429s around 00:05 UTC during our nightly ingestion. Only happening for streaming chat endpoints (we stream assistant replies). Example request-id: r-98b2c3f. A lot of the failures are immediate 429s, not timeouts.
Avery (Support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a compact curl or SDK call and the response headers when you get the 429? Also which region + model?
Maya (GaleHealth): region=eu-west-1, model=redwood-3-small, SDK v1.2.3. Here's a small repro (we use HTTP/2 multiplexing + keep-alive + many concurrent streams):
```
# simplified repro (node fetch over http2 multiplex)
POST /v1/stream/chat HTTP/2
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{ "model": "redwood-3-small", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"sync payload"}], "stream": true }
```
Maya (GaleHealth): sample response headers from a 429: `HTTP/2 429`
`x-request-id: r-98b2c3f`
`x-rate-limit-limit: 600 TPM`
`x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`
`x-rate-limit-reset: 23`
`retry-after: 1`
Avery (Support): Thanks — that headers set clarifies it's a TPM throttle (remaining=0). Two quick clarifications: are you batching a lot of short-turn messages at once? Also does each client maintain long-lived connections with many parallel streams?
Maya (GaleHealth): yep — our ingestion fanout spins up ~60 parallel streams per worker for a bursty sync window. Usually RPM is fine but TPM jumps because some turns are long (we sometimes send large context for system messages).
Jin (Oncall): FYI this pattern looks like token-cost churn: a few long prompts in the same minute can push you over the TPM even if request count is modest. TPM is tokens-per-minute, not requests-per-minute.
Sasha (Infra): Can you grab a short tail of logs for r-98b2c3f? I'm curious if the 429s align with a couple of multi-thousand-token responses. If so, short-term mitigations: reduce concurrent streams per connection, add jittered client-side rate-limiting, or switch to sequential streaming for the big-turn flows.
Maya (GaleHealth): logs attached (trimmed):
```
[00:04:58] req=r-98b2c3f model=redwood-3-small tok_in=420 tok_out_est=2100 duration=0.9s status=200
[00:05:03] req=r-98b2d11a model=redwood-3-small tok_in=380 tok_out_est=2900 duration=1.2s status=200
[00:05:04] req=r-98b2f00b model=redwood-3-small tok_in=120 tok_out_est=120 tok_cache=40 duration=0.2s status=429
[00:05:04] req=r-98b2c3f model=redwood-3-small status=429 note="tpm-exceeded"
```
Avery (Support): That confirms it — a few ~3k-token outputs inside the same minute pushed token consumption above your TPM. Two paths: (1) immediate: apply client-side smoothing to ensure token rate stays under the limit (leaky bucket or token-bucket with per-minute capacity) and lower concurrent streams for heavy prompts; (2) short-term: we can open a temporary TPM increase for the account while you roll out smoothing. Which do you want?
Maya (GaleHealth): can we get a temporary bump? This sync has SLAs. Also any quick SDK toggles we can flip server-side to avoid code changes?
Sasha (Infra): On Hosted we have a "burst_capacity" guard for some customers on dedicated plans; for hosted we can enable a short grace window (effectively allowing small token bursts) but it's gated. I'll check eligibility. Meanwhile you can enable a cheap mitigation: cap `max_concurrent_streams` to 8 per worker and add 25–50ms random stagger between new streams — no code-heavy change.
Avery (Support): Opening internal request — ticket S-2026-1141. ops-bot: created incident ticket S-2026-1141 for TPM surge — assign infra.
ops-bot: Incident created: S-2026-1141 · TPM surge for GaleHealth. Assignee: @Sasha (Infra). Priority: P2.
Sasha (Infra): I checked — account is on hosted tier, not Dedicated, so we can do a temporary 2x TPM soft bump for 3 hours while you deploy client smoothing. Want me to enable now?
Maya (GaleHealth): please enable. We'll deploy smoothing changes in ~30m. Thanks.
Avery (Support): Done — enabled soft bump to 1200 TPM for 3h, noted in ticket. Keep an eye on `x-rate-limit-remaining`. If you still see 429s after smoothing, paste a new sample.
Maya (GaleHealth): after capping streams + 50ms stagger we dropped from ~45 429s/min to 1-2. Looks stable. Thanks. :thumbsup:
Jin (Oncall): long-term recs: 1) instrument token-cost estimates client-side (we have cost-estimation doc link: https://docs.redwood.ai/optimize/token-costs) 2) consider Dedicated if sync windows will be sustained at high token rates 3) prefer prefix/KV caching for repeated system context to lower token out.
Maya (GaleHealth): appreciated — we'll follow up on Dedicated evaluation. Closing on our side once we verify nightly run tomorrow.
Avery (Support): Happy to help — keeping ticket S-2026-1141 open until you confirm.
Maya (GaleHealth): confirmed next-day run passed with zero 429s during the window. closing. thanks everyone.
